about: Hunahpu and Xbalanque go down to Xibalba, each with his blowgun. They go down the steep steps in an instant, cross the rushing water of a ravine between birds called Molai, and cross the rivers Puhia and Quiquia, the river of pus and the river of blood, where Xibalba means to catch them; they do not wade, but cross on their blowguns, and come out at the crossing of four roads, black, white, red and green. They already know the roads of Xibalba, and they send ahead a creature called the Xan to bite the seated figures one by one. The first two, an effigy and a figure of carved wood, say nothing; the third is Huncame, who cries out, and from then on each lord who is bitten cries out and the one beside him calls him by name and asks what has bitten him, until all the lords have named one another. It was no true Xan but a hair Hunahpu had pulled from his shin. So when the twins arrive they will not greet the effigy and the wooden figure, and they greet the twelve lords by name, every one. They will not sit on the bench, which is a hot stone, and they are sent to the Dark House, the first trial of Xibalba. There they are given a lit torch and cigars, to be given back whole at dawn: they put the red tail feathers of a macaw in place of the flame and fireflies on the tips of the cigars, and the watchers are fooled all night. The lords marvel: who fathered these boys, who bore them? Then they call them to the ball game. The boys will not say where they come from. The two sides argue over whose ball is to be used, the lords' rubber ball or a head. The lords throw first, and a white flint comes out of the ball and goes clattering over the court. The boys protest: is it death you want for us? Then we are going.

sentences.t: Ta xe be cut huhun chi vvb chique, xe cah chi Xibalba.
sentences.l: Then they-went then each with his-blowgun to-them, they-went-down to Xibalba.
sentences.i: Then they went, each with his blowgun, and went down to Xibalba.
sentences.n: Brasseur begins his eighth chapter here. xe be 'they went' (be 'go'). huhun chi vvb chique 'each with his blowgun': huhun 'each, one by one' (hun 'one' doubled); vvb is v- 'his' + vb 'blowgun' (house table), as earlier parts write it; chique 'to them', here 'for each of them'. xe cah 'they went down': cah is the verb 'go down' (toggle qaj), not cah 'sky'. The twins have just planted their canes in the middle of the house (end of the last part).

sentences.t: Libah chi xe cah chua cumuc; xe icou chi vi cut chupan halha zivan, xa chuxol ꜯiquin xe icou vi; are ri ꜯiquin Molai qui bi.
sentences.l: Instantly they-went-down at-its-face cumuc(?); they-passed again there then inside rushing-water(?) ravine, only among birds they-passed there; this the birds, Molai their name.
sentences.i: In an instant they went down the steep steps (?); they passed through the rushing water (?) of a ravine, passing between birds, birds whose name is Molai.
sentences.n: Libah chi 'in an instant', as in 010 (libah chi xe vlic). chua cumuc: the MS looks like camuc, and it is read cumuc with Brasseur (cumuk) and 010's vchi cumuc, a doubtful reading. chua is chi + v- 'its' + a, 'at the face of' (as chuva 'in front of'); Brasseur prints chuva here, and the establishment log does not discuss the difference. cumuc is not otherwise known; 'steep steps' follows Brasseur ('les gradins précipités', the stepped descent of the mountain) and is a guess; the toggle respells the letters. xe icou 'they passed' (icou, toggle ik'ow). chi vi cut: chi is chic 'again' without its c, as in 010's parallel xe eco chi cut chupan (toggle chik, as there). halha zivan 'the rushing water of the ravine': halha is taken as 010's hal ha, hal 'change, move' + ha 'water' (Brasseur 'eaux bouillonnantes'; inferred); zivan 'ravine, gorge'. chuxol 'among' (chi + v- + xol). The Molai birds are known only from this line; Brasseur's note asks what bird it was. The name is kept and respelled.

sentences.t: Xe icou chicut pa Puhia, pa Quiquia, chacbal ta que chi qui ꜭux Xibalba; mavi xqui yicou, xa chirih vvb xe icou vi.
sentences.l: They-passed again-then at Puhia, at Quiquia, means-of-defeating (ta) them in their heart Xibalba; not they-waded(?)-it, only on-the-back-of his-blowgun they-passed there.
sentences.i: Then they crossed at Puhia and at Quiquia, the rivers of pus and of blood, which were to be their downfall, as Xibalba had it in mind; they did not wade across, but crossed on the backs of their blowguns.
sentences.n: Puhia and Quiquia are rivers: puh 'pus' and quic 'blood' with ia, which Brasseur takes as ya 'water, river' (Pa-puh-ya 'in the river of mud, pus'; Quiq-ya 'river of blood'); the names are kept, and the English adds their meanings. In 010 the fathers crossed a river of blood (chi quiqui a). chacbal 'means of defeating': chac 'defeat, beat' (009) + -bal, the noun of means or place (inferred; toggle chakb'al). que 'them', the twins. chi qui ꜭux Xibalba 'in the heart of Xibalba', in their intention (the g-shaped letter is ꜭ, Brasseur qux). xqui yicou is read as the icou 'pass' verb with qui- 'they' and a y before the vowel: 'they did not cross them' (Brasseur x-qui yiqou, with his q for ꜭ, as in his iqou; 'ils n'y touchèrent pas du pied'; inferred; the toggle follows the published ik'ow). xa chirih vvb 'on the back of the blowgun': chirih, chi + r- 'its' + ih 'back'. The singular is written; the English makes it plural.

sentences.t: Xe el chicu apanoc pa cahib xalcat be.
sentences.l: They-came-out again-then over-there at four crossing road.
sentences.i: Then they came out again, over there, at the crossing of four roads.
sentences.n: xe el 'they came out' (el 'go out'). chicu 'again then'. apanoc 'away, over there' after a verb of motion: apan + -oc. pa cahib xalcat be 'at the crossing of four roads', the phrase of 010 (xalcat 'crossing, fork', inferred there).

sentences.t: Xa xquetaam vi cut qui be Xibalba: queca be, zaqui be, caca be, raxa be.
sentences.l: Just they-knew there then their roads Xibalba: black road, white road, red road, green road.
sentences.i: But they already knew the roads of Xibalba: the black road, the white road, the red road, the green road.
sentences.n: xquetaam 'they knew': x- + qu- (qui- 'they' before a vowel) + etaam 'know'. qui be Xibalba 'the roads of Xibalba', be singular in form. The four colour words take -a: queca 'black' (queꜫ, the root of queꜫum 'darkness'; toggle q'eqa, as in 010), zaqui 'white' (with -i), caca 'red', raxa 'green'. caca is written here with two plain c, where 010 has ꜫaꜫa be; the word is 'red' (Brasseur Caka be, 'le chemin Rouge'), the modern kaq, so the toggle gives kaqa (the c read as q, no ejective added). In 010 the fourth road was yellow (ꜫana); here it is green. The fathers did not know the roads and were brought low at this crossing; the twins knew them.

sentences.t: Chiri cut xqui tac vi hun chicop, Xan v bi; are camol qui ta xqui tac vbic.
sentences.l: There then they-sent there one animal, Xan its name; this taker their hearing they-sent away.
sentences.i: From there they sent on a creature, whose name was the Xan; they sent it on ahead to bring back what they would hear (?).
sentences.n: xqui tac 'they sent' (tac 'send'). chicop 'animal, creature'. Xan v bi 'Xan its name': the Xan is a biting creature whose share, in the next sentence, is to suck people's blood; in the dictionaries xan is a mosquito (inferred). The name is kept in English, as the text names it. camol qui ta is a doubtful reading and division: camol is written with plain c (Brasseur qamol), and is taken as cam 'take' + -ol, the agent noun of 010's camol que 'the ones to take us' (toggle k'amol); qui ta 'their hearing', from ta 'hear'. Brasseur: 'it was to gather the news they sent it to fetch'; the English follows that sense (inferred). vbic 'away, thither'.

sentences.t: “Huhunal que a tio; nabe cha ti ri nabe cubulel, cha ꜩaconizah qui tiic conohel; xa vech vi cut cha ꜩubah vi v quiquel vinac pa be,” xuꜭhaxic ri Xan.
sentences.l: “Each-one them you-bite; first you-bite the first seated-one, you-finish(?) their biting all; only mine(?) there then you-suck there its-blood people on road,” was-told the Xan.
sentences.i: “Bite them one by one: bite the first one seated first, and finish by biting them all (?); and then your share (?) shall be to suck the blood of people on the roads,” the Xan was told.
sentences.n: Huhunal que a tio 'one by one you bite them': huhunal 'each one' (huhun + -al); que 'them' (c-, the ongoing mark, + e 'them'); a- 'you (one)'; tio is ti 'bite' + -o, the ending of a transitive verb (in earlier parts ti, tio 'eat (flesh)'; here 'bite', Brasseur 'Mord-les'). cha ti 'bite!': ch- (command) + a- 'you' + ti; in cha ti ri, tiic and xu ti (next units) the t is written like an h, as in 017, and is read t with Brasseur. cubulel 'seated ones': cubul 'seated' + -el. cha ꜩaconizah is a doubtful reading (Brasseur ch'a izakonizah): the word is written with the crossed ꜩ first and a plain z later; 'finish' follows Brasseur ('finis par les mordre tous') and is a guess, and the toggle respells the letters. qui tiic 'their biting', the -ic noun of ti. xa vech is a doubtful reading (Brasseur x'av'ech): vech is v- 'my' + ech 'possession', 'mine', as written; Brasseur's division gives 'your share', and the English takes that sense (inferred). cha ꜩubah 'suck' (Brasseur prints chi tzubah; the establishment log does not discuss it): the modern tz'ub' 'suck', so the toggle gives tz'ub'aj (as ꜩonoh is tz'onoj). v quiquel vinac 'the blood of people' (quiquel 'blood'). xuꜭhaxic 'he was told': xu- + ꜭhax, the passive of ꜭha 'say' + -ic.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala,” xꜭha curi Xan.
sentences.l: “Good bala,” it-said then-the Xan.
sentences.i: “Very well,” said the Xan.
sentences.n: Vꜩ bala 'very well' (house table). xꜭha curi Xan: the next page begins ꜭha curi, and the x is read in the flourish after vꜩ bala at the foot of the page before (doubtful); the r of curi is written like a v (Brasseur curi). curi is cut 'then' + ri 'the' run together.

sentences.t: Ta xoc pa queca be; tacal cu chirih ri poy, aham che, nabe culel, e cautalic.
sentences.l: Then it-entered by black road; set then on the effigy, carved wood, first seated-one(s), they set-up(?).
sentences.i: Then it went in by the black road; it came to rest on the effigy and the figure of carved wood, the first ones seated there, set up in their places (?).
sentences.n: xoc 'it went in' (oc 'enter'), the Xan; queca be 'the black road', the road that in 010 spoke and led the fathers to their downfall. tacal 'come to rest, alighting' (as 010's e cu tacal chuvi hom, of the owls), here with no x-. chirih 'on' (on the back of). poy, aham che 'the effigy, the carved wood' (house table), the figures the fathers greeted as lords in 010. culel is taken as 'seated one', in step with the cubulel of the last unit (in this paragraph the text has culel thirteen times and cubulel once); a short form of cubulel, or another word, is not certain (inferred; toggle by the letters). cautalic as in 010, 'set up, arranged' after Brasseur (a guess); here Brasseur renders it 'couverts de leurs ornements', 'in their finery'.

sentences.t: Nabe cut xqui tio; mavi xꜭhavic. Xu ti chicu, ta xu ti chi v cab culel; ma chi vi xꜭhavic.
sentences.l: First then they-bit; not it-spoke. It-bit again-then, then it-bit (chi) its-second seated-one; not again (vi) it-spoke.
sentences.i: First it bit; there was no word. Then it bit again, it bit the second one seated; again there was no word.
sentences.n: Two matching sentences: a bite, then mavi xꜭhavic 'it did not speak' … ma chi vi xꜭhavic 'again it did not speak' (chi is chic 'again' without its c; toggle chik). xꜭhavic 'it spoke': x- + ꜭhau 'speak' (the v is u) + -ic. xqui tio is written with qui- 'they', though the Xan is one (perhaps for the twins, who sent it; the English keeps the Xan as the biter). In xqui tio and xu ti the t is written like an h, read t with Brasseur. xu ti 'it bit': xu- 'it' (singular) + ti. v cab culel 'the second seated one': v- 'its' + cab 'two', the ordinal (as in modern ukab').

sentences.t: Xu ti chicu rox; ca chi rox culel ꜭo vi Huncame.
sentences.l: It-bit again-then third; ca (chi) third seated-one, there-is there Huncame.
sentences.i: It bit the third; and the third one seated, there sat Huncame.
sentences.n: rox 'third', the ordinal of oxib 'three'. ca chi rox is a doubtful reading and division (Brasseur ca chi r'ox): ca is left unrendered, as in 010, and chi is perhaps chic 'again'. ꜭo vi 'is there': ꜭo 'be (in a place)' + vi 'there'; the g-shaped letter is ꜭ (Brasseur qo). Huncame 'One Death' is the first lord of Xibalba (009).

sentences.t: “Aqui!” xꜭha cut hun ta xtiic. “Ahi!” xꜭha Huncame.
sentences.l: “Aqui!” he-said then one when he-was-bitten. “Ahi!” he-said Huncame.
sentences.i: “Aqui!” cried one when he was bitten. “Ahi!” said Huncame.
sentences.n: Aqui and Ahi are cries of pain, kept in K'iche' in the English (Brasseur 'Ah! ay!'). xtiic 'he was bitten': x- + ti 'bite' + -ic. Here the manuscript has a naqui struck out in Ximénez's own pale ink before Ahi xꜭha Huncame; a later reader's dark bracket (probably Brasseur's) seems to mark Ahi xꜭha Huncame for omission, and Brasseur prints nothing there. Ximénez went on to write the words, so they are printed. The one who cries Aqui may be Huncame himself.

sentences.t: “Naqui, Huncame? Naquila mi xi tiouic? Xa hina quichila mi xi tiouic?” xꜭha chic v cab culel.
sentences.l: “What, Huncame? What just it-bit-you? Only hina(?) quichila(?) just it-bit-you?” he-said again its-second seated-one.
sentences.i: “What is it, Huncame? What has bitten you? Is it some thing or other (?) that has bitten you?” said the next one seated.
sentences.n: Naqui 'what (is it)'; naquila 'what (is it) there': naqui + la, as in 016. mi 'just now' before a completed verb. xi tiouic 'it has bitten you': x- + i + tiou, ti 'bite' with -ou, the form in which the biter is the one asked about ('what is it that bit') + -ic; the same form is xe tiouic 'that bit them' in ¶4. The i is read 'you' with Brasseur ('quoi donc vous a piqué'): perhaps ix 'you (pl.)', said in respect, with its x not written (inferred). Here and in every xi tiouic the t is written like an h. Xa hina quichila is a doubtful reading and is not understood: Brasseur prints Xahina quichina and gives it to Huncame as his answer, 'something I do not know', where the manuscript has mi xi tiouic and the tag of the next seated one. The English is a guess, and the toggle respells the letters. v cab culel 'the second seated one': by the count this is the fourth (Vucub Came, who asks after Huncame), and Brasseur reads u cah culel 'the fourth'; the manuscript has cab 'second' (printed as written), and the English says only 'the next one'.

sentences.t: “Naqui, Vvcub Came? Naquila mi xi tiouic?” xꜭha chi roo culel.
sentences.l: “What, Vvcub Came? What just it-bit-you?” he-said again fifth seated-one.
sentences.i: “What is it, Vucub Came? What has bitten you?” said the fifth one seated.
sentences.n: Vvcub Came 'Seven Death', the second lord (009; the English spells Vucub). chi roo culel 'the fifth seated one': the r is written like a v (MS chivoo), read r with Brasseur (r'oo); roo is the ordinal 'fifth', as 011's Roo 'its fifth' (inferred; the doubled o may mark a glottal stop, and the toggle respells the letters, as 011). chi is chic 'again' without its c, as the xꜭha chic of the other tags (toggle chik). The fifth one is Xiquiripat, named in the next unit. The pattern from here on: each one bitten cries out, and the one beside him asks him what is wrong, calling him by name.

sentences.t: “Ahi, ahi!” xꜭha na Xiquiripat. Xꜭha Vvcub Came chire: “Naquila mi xi tiouic?” xꜭha chic; xtiic v vacac culel: “Ahi!”
sentences.l: “Ahi, ahi!” he-said then Xiquiripat. He-said Vvcub Came to-him: “What just it-bit-you?” he-said again; he-was-bitten its-sixth seated-one: “Ahi!”
sentences.i: “Ahi, ahi!” cried Xiquiripat then. Vucub Came said to him: “What has bitten you?” he said in his turn; and the sixth one seated was bitten: “Ahi!”
sentences.n: na 'then, now'. Xiquiripat is a lord of the blood (009). chire 'to him'. v vacac culel 'the sixth seated one': vacac is the ordinal of 'six' (toggle waqaq, after the modern waqib 'six'). Brasseur rearranges the speakers in this stretch and adds cries the manuscript does not have; the manuscript is followed, and the quotation marks are ours, one reasonable division.

sentences.t: “Naqui, Cuchumaquic?” xꜭha Xiquiripat chire. “Naquila mi xi tiouic?” xꜭha chic, ta xti v vvc culel. “Ahi!” xꜭha chic.
sentences.l: “What, Cuchumaquic?” he-said Xiquiripat to-him. “What just it-bit-you?” he-said again, when was-bitten its-seventh seated-one. “Ahi!” he-said again.
sentences.i: “What is it, Cuchumaquic?” Xiquiripat said to him. “What has bitten you?” he went on, as the seventh one seated was bitten. “Ahi!” he cried.
sentences.n: Cuchumaquic, the other lord of the blood (009), the father of Xquic (012). xti, x- + ti, with no person written, so passive in sense, as xtiic in U15: 'when the seventh was bitten' (Brasseur 'au moment où il était également piqué'; the t written like an h, read t with Brasseur). v vvc culel 'the seventh seated one': vvc is the ordinal of vvcub 'seven' (toggle wuq). As written, the second question closes with xꜭha chic 'he said again', as Vucub Came's question in U15 does, so it is read as the same asker going on; Brasseur gives it instead to the next seated one, as he is bitten ('ajouta celui qui était assis le septième, au moment où il était également piqué').

sentences.t: “Naqui, Ahalpuh?” xꜭha Cuchumaquic chire. “Naquila mi xi tiouic?” xꜭha chic, ta xti chic v vahxac culel. “Ahi!” xꜭha chic.
sentences.l: “What, Ahalpuh?” he-said Cuchumaquic to-him. “What just it-bit-you?” he-said again, when was-bitten again its-eighth seated-one. “Ahi!” he-said again.
sentences.i: “What is it, Ahalpuh?” Cuchumaquic said to him. “What has bitten you?” he went on, as the eighth one seated was bitten. “Ahi!” he cried.
sentences.n: Ahalpuh, the lord of pus (009). v vahxac culel 'the eighth seated one' (vahxac, the ordinal of 'eight'; toggle wajxaq). chic 'again' marks the next in the series.

sentences.t: “Naqui, Ahalcana?” xꜭha chi Ahalpuh chire. “Naquila mi xi tiouic?” ꜭha chic, ta xti chic v beleh culel. “Ahi!” xꜭha.
sentences.l: “What, Ahalcana?” he-said again Ahalpuh to-him. “What just it-bit-you?” says again, when was-bitten again its-ninth seated-one. “Ahi!” he-said.
sentences.i: “What is it, Ahalq'ana?” Ahalpuh said to him. “What has bitten you?” he went on, as the ninth one seated was bitten. “Ahi!” he cried.
sentences.n: Ahalcana is written with plain c, as in 010, where 009 printed Ahalꜫana with the tresillo (Brasseur Ahalcana); as 010 did, the English and the toggle keep 009's form for the same lord (Ahalq'ana, Ajalq'ana). ꜭha chic: the tag is written without x- (here and in ¶3's Naqui? ꜭha chic), as in the manuscript; 'says'. v beleh culel 'the ninth seated one' (beleh, the ordinal of 'nine'; toggle b'elej).

sentences.t: “Naqui, Chamiabac?” xꜭha Ahalcana chire. “Naquila mi xi tiouic?” xꜭha chic, ta xti chic v lahuh cubulel. “Ahi!”
sentences.l: “What, Chamiabac?” he-said Ahalcana to-him. “What just it-bit-you?” he-said again, when was-bitten again its-tenth seated-one. “Ahi!”
sentences.i: “What is it, Chamiabac?” Ahalq'ana said to him. “What has bitten you?” he went on, as the tenth one seated was bitten. “Ahi!”
sentences.n: Chamiabac 'Bone Staff', one of the two staff-bearers of Xibalba (009). v lahuh cubulel 'the tenth seated one': lahuh 'ten' (toggle lajuj); here the full cubulel is written.

sentences.t: “Naqui, Chamiaholom?” xꜭha Chamiabac. “Naquila mi xi tiouic?” xꜭha chic, ta xti chic v hulah culel. “Ahi!” xꜭha chic.
sentences.l: “What, Chamiaholom?” he-said Chamiabac. “What just it-bit-you?” he-said again, when was-bitten again its-eleventh seated-one. “Ahi!” he-said again.
sentences.i: “What is it, Chamiaholom?” said Chamiabac. “What has bitten you?” he went on, as the eleventh one seated was bitten. “Ahi!” he cried.
sentences.n: Chamiaholom 'Skull Staff', the other staff-bearer (009). v hulah culel 'the eleventh seated one': hulah, the ordinal of hulahuh 'eleven' (toggle julaj, by the letters).

sentences.t: “Naqui?” ꜭha chic Chamiaholom chire. “Naquila mi xi tiouic?” xꜭha chic, ta xti chic v cablahuh culel. “Ahi!” xꜭha chic.
sentences.l: “What?” says again Chamiaholom to-him. “What just it-bit-you?” he-said again, when was-bitten again its-twelfth seated-one. “Ahi!” he-said again.
sentences.i: “What is it?” Chamiaholom said to him. “What has bitten you?” he went on, as the twelfth one seated was bitten. “Ahi!” he cried.
sentences.n: Here the one who asks gives no name: the eleventh lord is not named in the roll-call (Brasseur's note: 'the eleventh, the text says, without giving his name'). ꜭha chic, without x-, as written. v cablahuh culel 'the twelfth seated one': cablahuh, cab 'two' + lahuh 'ten' (toggle kab'lajuj).

sentences.t: “Naqui, Patan?” xꜭha chic chire. “Naquila mi xi tiouic?” xꜭha chic, ta xti chic roxlahuh culel. “Ahi!”
sentences.l: “What, Patan?” he-said again to-him. “What just it-bit-you?” he-said again, when was-bitten again thirteenth seated-one. “Ahi!”
sentences.i: “What is it, Patan?” the next said to him. “What has bitten you?” he went on, as the thirteenth one seated was bitten. “Ahi!”
sentences.n: Patan is one of the lords of 009, of sudden death on the road, paired there with Xic. The speaker is not named; the English supplies 'the next'. roxlahuh 'the thirteenth', r- + oxlahuh 'thirteen' (ox 'three' + lahuh), written without v- (toggle roxlajuj).

sentences.t: “Naqui, Quicxic?” ꜭha Patan chirech. “Naquila mi xi tiouic?” xꜭha chic, ta xti chic v cahlahuh culel. “Ahi!”
sentences.l: “What, Quicxic?” says Patan to-him. “What just it-bit-you?” he-said again, when was-bitten again its-fourteenth seated-one. “Ahi!”
sentences.i: “What is it, Quicxic?” Patan said to him. “What has bitten you?” he went on, as the fourteenth one seated was bitten. “Ahi!”
sentences.n: Quicxic is a lord not named in 009; Brasseur's note takes the name as quic 'blood' + xic 'hawk', 'Hawk Blood' (inferred), and notes that in place of 009's Ahalmez, Ahaltocob and Xic this list has Quicxic, Quicre and Quicrixcac. The name is kept, and the toggle respells the letters, as for the other lords' names. chirech 'to him', chi + r- + ech. v cahlahuh culel 'the fourteenth seated one' (cah 'four' + lahuh; toggle kajlajuj).

sentences.t: “Naquila mi xi tiouic?” xꜭha chic Quicrixcac; xꜭha Quicre chirech.
sentences.l: “What just it-bit-you?” he-said again Quicrixcac; he-said Quicre to-him.
sentences.i: “What has bitten you?” said Quicrixcac in his turn; Quicre said it to him.
sentences.n: The roll-call ends with the last two lords. Quicrixcac is quic 'blood' + r- 'its' + ixcac 'nail, claw', and Quicre quic + re 'teeth', after Brasseur's note ('Blood of the Claws or Nails', 'Blood of the Teeth'; inferred); both names are kept. As written, Quicrixcac speaks and Quicre speaks to him; Brasseur makes Quicrixcac the one addressed ('Qui donc vous a piqué, Quiqrixgag, lui dit Quiqre'). The two tags are printed as the manuscript has them.

sentences.t: Quehe cut v bixic qui bi ri xqui biyh conohel chi quibil quib;
sentences.l: Thus then its-saying their names which they-said all among themselves;
sentences.i: So their names were spoken: all of them said them to one another;
sentences.n: v bixic 'its being said': bix, the passive of biyh 'say', + -ic. xqui biyh 'they said' (biyh, as in earlier parts). chi quibil quib 'among themselves, to one another': quib 'themselves' with quibil.

sentences.t: xqui cut v vach, xqui biyh qui bi, huhun chi holoman v bixic cumal; are chi biyh v bi hun ri cubul chu xucut.
sentences.l: they-showed its-face, they-said their names, each (chi) holoman(?) its-saying by-them; this that he-says its-name one the seated at-its side.
sentences.i: they showed their faces, they said their names, each one's name spoken by them, head by head (?): each was to say the name of the one who sat at his side.
sentences.n: A couplet: xqui cut v vach, xqui biyh qui bi 'they showed their faces, they said their names'. cut is here the verb 'show' (modern k'ut), not cut 'then'; the word division xqui cut v vach is ours. holoman is not otherwise known; perhaps holom 'head' + -an, of the heads of Xibalba, or 'each in turn' (guess; Brasseur 'each of those who commanded there'). cumal 'by them'. are chi biyh 'this, to say': chi + biyh with no person written (no chu- 'he'), so 'to say' rather than 'that he say' (inferred). cubul chu xucut 'seated at his side': xucut 'side, corner' (the root of 001's xucutaxic); Brasseur reads 'the name of the last one, who sat in the corner' ('le nom du dernier qui était assis dans le coin'), and the English takes 'side' (inferred).

sentences.t: Mahabi hun oc xqui zach v bi; quiz qui biyh qui bi conohel, ta xe ti rumal rizmal v vach v chec Hunahpu, xu mich vbic.
sentences.l: Not-was one (oc) they-lost its-name; finished they-said their names all, when they-were-bitten by its-hair its-face his-shin Hunahpu, he-plucked away.
sentences.i: Not one name did they leave out; they finished saying all their names, as they were bitten by a hair from the front of Hunahpu's shin, which he had plucked out.
sentences.n: Mahabi hun oc 'not one': mahabi 'there is not' + hun 'one' + oc. xqui zach 'they lost, left out' (zach 'lose'). quiz qui biyh 'they finished saying': quiz 'finish', as an adverb before the verb. xe ti 'they were bitten' (the t written like an h, as above). rizmal v vach v chec 'the hair of the front of his shin': r- 'its' + izmal 'hair'; v vach 'its face, its front'; chec is taken as the leg (Brasseur 'le poil de la jambe'), perhaps the modern ch'ek 'knee'; the toggle respells the letters. xu mich 'he plucked out' (Brasseur 'que celui-ci s'arracha'; the modern mich' 'pluck', not restored). vbic 'away, off'. The Xan was a hair from Hunahpu's leg.

sentences.t: Mana quiꜩih Xan ri xe tiouic; xbe tao qui bi conohel rumal Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.l: Not true Xan the-one it-bit-them; it-went heard their names all for Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.i: It was no true Xan that bit them; it went to hear all their names for Hunahpu and Xbalanque.
sentences.n: Mana quiꜩih 'not truly, not a real'. xe tiouic 'that bit them': x- + e 'them' + tiou + -ic, the form in which the biter is the focus, as xi tiouic in the roll-call. xbe tao 'it went (and) heard': be 'go' + ta 'hear' + -o, the transitive ending. rumal 'by, for the sake of': here the Xan's errand was for the twins.

sentences.t: Catecut ta xebec, ta xe opon puch chila e ꜭo vi Xibalba.
sentences.l: Then when they-went, when they-arrived also there they there-are there Xibalba.
sentences.i: Then they set off, and came to the place where the lords of Xibalba were.
sentences.n: xebec 'they went', one word here (xe + bec). xe opon 'they arrived there'. chila 'there'. e ꜭo vi 'where they are': e 'they' + ꜭo 'be (in a place)' + vi 'there'; the g-shaped letter is ꜭ (Brasseur do, OCR for qo).

sentences.t: “Chi quihila ahau,” xꜭha ri cubulic, xꜭha hun tacchiinel.
sentences.l: “You-greet lord,” he-said the seated-one, he-said one tacchiinel(?).
sentences.i: “Greet the lord,” said one who sat there, a tempter (?).
sentences.n: Chi quihila 'greet!': ch- (command) + i- 'you (pl.)' + quihila 'greet, pay honour', as in 010 (inferred there). ahau 'lord'. cubulic 'seated', the -ic form of cubul. ri cubulic is taken as the speaker, 'the one seated'; Brasseur takes it as the one to be greeted ('Adorez le roi, leur dit-on, celui qui est là assis'), with xꜭha as 'they were told'. Either is possible from the words. tacchiinel is a doubtful reading: the first letter has the crossed loop of Ximénez's t, but it may be l (Brasseur lakchiinel). The word is not otherwise known; Brasseur renders 'to tempt them', and 'a tempter' follows him (a guess). The toggle respells the letters. The trick is the one that caught the fathers in 010, who greeted the effigy and the wooden figure as lords.

sentences.t: “Mavi are ahau ri, xa poy, aham che ri,” xeꜭha ta xe oponic.
sentences.l: “Not this lord that, only effigy, carved wood that,” they-said when they-arrived.
sentences.i: “That is no lord: that is only an effigy, a figure of carved wood,” they said as they came up.
sentences.n: Mavi are ahau ri 'that is not a lord': mavi 'not', are 'this, it', ri 'that'. poy, aham che 'effigy, carved wood' (house table). xe oponic 'they arrived there'.

sentences.t: Catecut ta xe calainic: “Calata Huncame; calata Vvcub Came; calata Xiquiripat; calata Cuchumaquic; calata Ahalpuh; calata Ahalcana; calata Chamiabac; calata Chamiaholom; calata Quicxic; calata Patan; calata Quicre; calata Quicrixcac,” xeꜭha ta xe oponic.
sentences.l: Then when they-greeted: “Hail (ta) Huncame; hail (ta) Vvcub Came; hail (ta) Xiquiripat; hail (ta) Cuchumaquic; hail (ta) Ahalpuh; hail (ta) Ahalcana; hail (ta) Chamiabac; hail (ta) Chamiaholom; hail (ta) Quicxic; hail (ta) Patan; hail (ta) Quicre; hail (ta) Quicrixcac,” they-said when they-arrived.
sentences.i: Then they greeted them: “Greetings, Huncame; greetings, Vucub Came; greetings, Xiquiripat; greetings, Cuchumaquic; greetings, Ahalpuh; greetings, Ahalq'ana; greetings, Chamiabac; greetings, Chamiaholom; greetings, Quicxic; greetings, Patan; greetings, Quicre; greetings, Quicrixcac,” they said as they came up.
sentences.n: The manuscript has calata cala xic, a misprint for calata Quicxic, corrected here: cala repeats the cala of calata, and the name is as written twice in the roll-call (Brasseur Quiqxic). calata is the greeting cala of 010 (Brasseur 'clear, bright, open', a wish that all be clear for the one greeted) + ta, the softening particle; calainic 'greet': cala + -in + -ic. The twelve lords go in pairs, as the list of 009 does. Two later-hand marks in dark ink are not taken in: a stroke before Ahalcana, and a heavy blot over two or three letters of Quicrixcac (MS Quic[..]rixcac); the letters under the blot cannot be read, and the name is printed as the roll-call writes it. Here Quicxic comes before Patan, the other way round from the roll-call.

sentences.t: Ronohel xquiz cut v vach, xqui biyh v bi ronohel; mahabi hun xqui zach v bi.
sentences.l: All it-was-finished then its-face, they-said its-name all; not-was one they-lost its-name.
sentences.i: They went through them all, face by face, and said every name; not one name did they leave out.
sentences.n: Ronohel 'all of it' (r- + onohel). xquiz cut v vach 'their faces were finished', that is, every face was gone through: xquiz is x- + quiz 'finish' with no qui- 'they', so intransitive, as in ¶7's habi xquiz ri chah 'the torch was not used up' (010 writes xqui quiz for 'they used up'); the sense is inferred (Brasseur 'leur découvrant à tous la face'). The rest repeats ¶4: xqui biyh v bi 'they said the name', mahabi hun xqui zach v bi 'not one name did they lose'.

sentences.t: Are ta xahauax chiquech, ma ta xcanai v bi cumal.
sentences.l: This (ta) it-was-wanted by-them, not (ta) it-was-found its-name by-them.
sentences.i: What the lords had wanted was that their names should not be found out by them.
sentences.n: xahauax 'it was wanted': x- + ah 'want' + -auax, a passive (the modern ajawax 'be wanted'; inferred). chiquech 'by them, to them', the lords. xcanai is not otherwise known; 'be found out' follows Brasseur ('que leurs noms n'eussent pas été découverts'), perhaps from can 'seek' (a guess; toggle by the letters). cumal 'by them', the twins. Part 019 begins with the same words, are ta cu xahauax chique.

sentences.t: “Quix cu vloc,” xe vꜭhax cut; xe rah oc chuvi tem; ma cu xcah.
sentences.l: “You-come then hither,” they-were-told then; them-it-wanted enter on-top bench; not then they-wanted.
sentences.i: “Come here, then,” they were told; they were meant to sit on the bench, but they would not.
sentences.n: Quix cu vloc 'come here, you (pl.)', the words of 010 (Quix cu vloc chuvi ca tem). xe vꜭhax 'they were told': vꜭhax, the passive of ꜭha with v-. xe rah oc chuvi tem 'they were wanted to go onto the bench': xe is the absolutive 'them' and r- the ergative 'it, he' before ah 'want', the fixed xrah construction of earlier parts, with the lords as the ones wanting; oc 'enter, get onto' (inferred; Brasseur 'le siège où ils désiraient qu'ils se missent'). tem 'bench' (010). ma cu xcah 'but they did not want': x- + c- (qui- 'they' before a vowel) + ah 'want' (toggle xkaj), not cah 'go down'.

sentences.t: “Mavi are catem ri, xa chohim abah ri tem,” xeꜭha Hunahpu, Xbalanque; mavi xe chacatahic.
sentences.l: “Not this our-bench that, only heated(?) stone that bench,” they-said Hunahpu, Xbalanque; not they-were-brought-low.
sentences.i: “That is not a bench for us: that bench is only a heated stone,” said Hunahpu and Xbalanque; and they were not brought low.
sentences.n: catem 'our bench': ca- 'our' + tem (Brasseur ka tem 'notre siège'), written as one word; the t is written like an f (MS cafem) and read t. chohim abah 'heated stone' (Brasseur chohim-abah, 'pierre chauffée'); chohim is not otherwise known (inferred; toggle by the letters). In 010 the fathers sat on this burning stone. mavi xe chacatahic 'they were not brought low': chacatah, the verb of 010.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala; xa ba hix pa ha,” xe vchaxic.
sentences.l: “Good bala; only (ba) go-you in house,” they-were-told.
sentences.i: “Very well: just go into the house,” they were told.
sentences.n: xa ba hix 'just go, you (pl.)': ba, the particle of urging; hix 'go, you (pl.)', as in 010 (Xa hix chi ha). The h of hix has the stroke Ximénez puts over h and t; it is read h with Brasseur (h'yx). pa ha 'into the house' (ha 'house'). xe vchaxic 'they were told', written here with plain ch (toggle uchaxik, as in earlier parts).

sentences.t: Catecut ta xe oc pa Queꜫuma Ha; mavi xe chacatahic chiri.
sentences.l: Then when they-entered in Dark House; not they-were-brought-low there.
sentences.i: Then they went into the Dark House, and they were not brought low there.
sentences.n: The manuscript has pa queꜫum maha, a misprint for pa Queꜫuma Ha, corrected here: the m is written twice across the word break, and the name is as written five lines above on the same page (and in 010). A later reader's dark underline stands under the first m. Queꜫuma Ha 'Dark House': queꜫum 'darkness' + -a, + ha 'house', the first of the houses of trial (house table; 010, 011). chiri 'there'.

sentences.t: Are nabe v tihobal Xibalba ri; xe oc vi que chi cu v ticaric qui chacatahic ta chic chi qui ꜭux Xibalba.
sentences.l: This first its-trial Xibalba that; they-entered there, (que) shall then its-beginning their being-brought-low (ta) now in their heart Xibalba.
sentences.i: That was the first trial of Xibalba: where they went in, their downfall was now to begin, as Xibalba had it in mind.
sentences.n: v tihobal 'its trial': tih 'try, test' + -obal (010). xe oc vi 'they entered there': vi points back to the place. que chi cu v ticaric 'their beginning shall then (be)': ticaric 'beginning', the tiquiba 'begin' of earlier parts with -ar + -ic (inferred); its t is written like an h (MS vh'icaric) and is read t with Brasseur. que is not clear here (perhaps 'thus' or 'them'). qui chacatahic 'their being brought low'. chi qui ꜭux Xibalba 'in the heart of Xibalba', as in ¶1: so Xibalba intended.

sentences.t: Nabe xe oc pa Queꜫuma Ha. Catecut ta xbe yaoc qui chah ca tilovic, ta xoponic ruꜭ huhun qui zic rumal vzamahel Huncame.
sentences.l: First they-entered in Dark House. Then when went to-be-given their torch burning, when it-arrived with each their cigar, by his-messenger Huncame.
sentences.i: First they went into the Dark House. Then their torch was brought to them, burning, and it came with a cigar for each of them, by the messenger of Huncame.
sentences.n: xbe yaoc 'it went to be given': be 'go' + ya 'give' + -oc, as in 010. chah 'torch', a splinter of resinous pine (010). ca tilovic 'burning': ca, the ongoing c-, + tilov + -ic, not otherwise known; 'burning, lit' follows Brasseur ('tout allumées'; a guess). The t is written like an h (MS cahilovic). ruꜭ 'with it'. huhun qui zic 'each one's cigar' (zic 'tobacco, cigar', toggle sik'). vzamahel 'his messenger': v- + zamahel. In 010 the fathers were given the same things.

sentences.t: “Vae qui chah e,” cacha ahau; “chul qui ya chic ri chah zacaric, ruꜭ ri zic chul qui moloba,” cacha ahau, xꜭha zamahel ta xoponic.
sentences.l: “This their torch they,” says lord; “let-come they-give again the torch at-dawn, with the cigar let-come they-gather(?)-it,” says lord, he-said messenger when he-arrived.
sentences.i: “Here is their torch,” says the lord; “at dawn they are to come and give the torch back, and with it the cigars: they are to come and bring them back,” says the lord: so the messenger said when he came.
sentences.n: The messenger gives the lord's words, with cacha ahau 'says the lord' (cacha with plain ch, toggle kacha, as in 017). Vae qui chah e 'here is their torch': vae 'this, here is'; e 'they', pointing to the boys (inferred). chul 'let (them) come': ch- + vl 'come here'. qui ya chic 'they give back': ya 'give' + chic 'again'. zacaric 'at dawn' (zac 'white, light'; 010 has zaquiric; toggle saqarik). moloba 'gather, bring back together' (010, inferred). In 010 the lords asked for the torch and cigars back whole (xavi xere v vach); here they say only 'bring them back'.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala,” xeꜭha cut.
sentences.l: “Good bala,” they-said then.
sentences.i: “Very well,” they said.
sentences.n: The twins answer with Vꜩ bala 'very well' (house table). xeꜭha 'they said': xe- 'they' + ꜭha.

sentences.t: Ma cu xqui ꜩih ri chah; xa ꜫaꜫa hu ꜫex v vach xoquic, are v he caquix; quehe ri chah xquilo varanel.
sentences.l: Not then they-lit the torch; only red one(?) exchange its-face it-went-in, this its-tail macaw; like the torch they-saw-it watchers.
sentences.i: But they did not light the torch: something red went in in its place, the tail feathers of the macaw, and the watchers took it for the torch.
sentences.n: xqui ꜩih 'they lit': ꜩih, here 'kindle, light', as 010's ꜩihom 'lit' (inferred). Brasseur prints Ma cu quitzih ri chah 'in truth … not the torch' here and supplies '(brûlèrent)' in his French; the manuscript has xqui ꜩih (the establishment log reads it 'light', as in ¶7's xqui ꜩih chire), and it is followed. xa ꜫaꜫa hu ꜫex v vach is a doubtful reading: the MS looks like xaꜫaꜫahu quexvach, and the first letter of the second word looks like q; Brasseur's g decided ꜫ (his xa caka hu gexvach). ꜫaꜫa 'red', as in 010; hu is taken as hun 'one, a' without its n (inferred); ꜫex 'exchange', the root of the vꜫexel 'replacement' of the house table, so ꜫex v vach 'in exchange for it' (inferred; Brasseur 'quelque chose de rouge à la place'). v he caquix 'the macaw's tail': he 'tail' (as qui he 'their tails' in earlier parts), caquix 'scarlet macaw' (the Caquix of Vucub Caquix). xquilo 'they saw it' (il 'see' + -o). varanel 'watchers': var 'sleep' + -an + -el, those who keep the night (Brasseur 'veilleurs'; inferred, toggle by the letters).

sentences.t: Are chi cu ri zic, xa ꜫaꜫa chicop xqui coho chuvi zic.
sentences.l: This again then the cigar, only fire animal they-put-it on-top cigar.
sentences.i: And for the cigars, they put fireflies on the tips of the cigars.
sentences.n: Are chi cu ri zic 'and as for the cigar': chi is chic 'again, next' without its c (toggle chik, as Are chi cu ri in 004 and Are chi curi in 009). xa ꜫaꜫa chicop 'only fire creatures': ꜫaꜫ 'fire' + -a, the same letters as ꜫaꜫa 'red' (Brasseur gaga, 'des lucioles', fireflies; inferred). xqui coho 'they put it' (coh 'put' + -o). chuvi zic 'on the top, the tip, of the cigar' (chuvi, chi + v- + vi 'head').

sentences.t: Hun aꜫab chi yocouic cumal. “Mi xe cachaco,” xeꜭha varanel.
sentences.l: One night (chi) watched(?) by-them. “Just them we-have-beaten,” they-said watchers.
sentences.i: All night they were watched over (?) by them. “We have beaten them,” said the watchers.
sentences.n: Hun aꜫab 'one night', a whole night: the MS looks like acab, and Brasseur's agab decided ꜫ (doubtful). chi yocouic is a doubtful reading, written with plain c (Brasseur yogouic); 'be watched over, guarded' follows Brasseur ('ils furent gardés'; a guess, toggle by the letters). cumal 'by them', the watchers. Mi xe cachaco 'we have just beaten them': mi 'just now' + x- + e 'them' + ca- 'we' + chac 'defeat' + -o, written as one word (Brasseur Mi-x-e ca chako, 'Ils sont tombés dans le piège').

sentences.t: Ma cu habi xquiz ri chah, xavi xere v vach; are cu ri zic, mahabi naquila xqui ꜩih chire, xavi xere v vach.
sentences.l: Not then there-was it-was-finished the torch, just thus its-face; this then the cigar, not-was what they-lit of-it, just thus its-face.
sentences.i: But the torch had not burned away: it looked just as before; and the cigars, not a bit of them had they lit: they looked just as before.
sentences.n: A couplet: the torch and the cigar, each closing with xavi xere v vach 'just so its face', looking as it did when it was given (as in 010, where the lords asked for them back so). Ma cu habi 'but there was not': habi 'there is not'. xquiz 'it was finished, used up' (quiz 'finish'). mahabi naquila xqui ꜩih chire 'nothing of it did they light'.

sentences.t: Xbe yaoc cuꜭ ahauab: “Naquipa que vxic? Apa xe pe vi? Achinac xe ꜭaholanic, xe alanic?
sentences.l: It-went to-be-given with-them lords: “What (pa) they becoming? Where they-came-from there? Who they-were-begotten, they-were-borne?
sentences.i: Torch and cigars were brought to the lords: “What sort of beings are these? Where have they come from? Who fathered them, who gave them birth?
sentences.n: cuꜭ ahauab 'to the lords': cuꜭ 'with them' (uꜭ 'company'). Naquipa que vxic 'what are they becoming', what manner of beings are they: naqui pa 'what' + que 'they' + vx 'become' + -ic. Apa xe pe vi 'where did they come from'. Achinac 'who' (plain c; Brasseur achinak, his k for q): the word is not otherwise known and the note cannot tie it to a known q word, so the toggle respells the letters (achinak), as 007 decided for such words. xe ꜭaholanic, xe alanic: the verbs of ꜭahol 'a man's son' and al 'a woman's child', 'they were fathered, they were borne', the pair of Alom and Ꜭaholom (house table), kept as a couplet.

sentences.t: Quiꜩih ca catat ca ꜭux rumal; ma vꜩ ca qui bano chique. Halan qui vach, halan nai pu qui ꜭoheic,” xeꜭha chi quibil quib.
sentences.l: Truly ongoing burning(?) our heart because-of-them; not good they-do to-us. Strange their face, strange also their being,” they-said among themselves.
sentences.i: Truly our hearts burn because of them; what they are doing to us is not good. Strange are their faces, and strange the way they are,” they said among themselves.
sentences.n: ca catat is a doubtful reading, written with plain c (Brasseur qatat): ca, the ongoing c-, + catat, read 'burning' with Brasseur ('notre cœur en est brûlant') and 016's chi catat … qui ꜭux (inferred; toggle by the letters). ca ꜭux 'our heart'. ma vꜩ ca qui bano chique 'it is not good, what they do to us': bano 'do it' (ban + -o); chique is here 'to us' (Brasseur 'avec nous'; toggle chiqe), the same letters as 'to them'. A couplet: halan qui vach, halan … qui ꜭoheic 'strange their faces, strange their being': halan 'strange, different', from hal 'change' (the modern jalan 'different'; inferred); ꜭoheic 'being, existence' (the g-shaped letter is ꜭ, Brasseur qoheic). nai pu 'likewise, also'.

sentences.t: Ta xe tacon cut conohel ahauab: “Oho chahoc, ix ꜭaholab,” xe vꜭhaxic.
sentences.l: Then they-sent then all lords: “Let's-go play(?), you boys,” they-were-told.
sentences.i: Then all the lords sent for them: “Come, let us play ball, boys,” they were told.
sentences.n: xe tacon 'they sent (for them)': tac 'send' + -on, the ending of a verb with no object written (inferred; Brasseur 'les envoyèrent chercher'). Oho 'come', as 017's cat oho 'come here' (inferred; Brasseur 'Allons'). chahoc 'to play (ball)': chah + -oc. It is written with one a, the letters of chah 'torch', where 'play' is chaah elsewhere (the next units); the toggle respells the letters. ix ꜭaholab 'you boys' (ꜭaholab, the plural of ꜭahol 'son').

sentences.t: Ta xe ꜩonox cut rumal Huncame, Vvcub Came: “Apa quix ix pe vi? Chi biyh tah, ix ꜭaholab,” xꜭha cut Xibalba chique.
sentences.l: Then they-were-asked then by Huncame, Vvcub Came: “Where you you come-from there? Tell (tah), you boys,” it-said then Xibalba to-them.
sentences.i: Then Huncame and Vucub Came questioned them: “Where do you come from? Tell us, boys,” Xibalba said to them.
sentences.n: xe ꜩonox 'they were asked': ꜩonox, the passive of ꜩonoh 'ask' (toggle tz'onox, as ꜩonoh is tz'onoj in 016 and 017). Apa quix ix pe vi 'where do you come from': apa 'where', quix 'you (pl.)' with the ongoing c-, ix 'you' again, pe 'come', vi 'there'. Chi biyh tah 'tell it, please': ch- + i- 'you (pl.)' + biyh 'say', tah the softening particle. xꜭha 'it said', Xibalba singular. After Xibalba the manuscript has mavi que|taam … xeꜭha with taam and xeꜭha struck through in dark ink (whose stroke is not certain); the struck words are not printed, and Brasseur omits them too.

sentences.t: “Alaba xoh pe vi lo; mavi quetaam,” xa xeꜭha; mavi xqui biyh.
sentences.l: “Alaba(?) we-came-from there perhaps; not we-know,” only they-said; not they-told.
sentences.i: “Who knows where we come from? We do not know,” was all they said; they did not tell.
sentences.n: Alaba is not otherwise known; 'who knows' follows Brasseur ('Qui saurait dire d'où nous venons?'; a guess, toggle by the letters). xoh pe vi 'we came from': x- + oh 'we' + pe 'come'. lo 'perhaps'. mavi quetaam 'we do not know': qu- for ca- 'we' before a vowel + etaam 'know' (toggle qetaam; the same letters are 'they know' elsewhere). xa xeꜭha 'only they said'.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala; xa ca beco ca chaah, ix ꜭaholab,” xeꜭha Xibalba chique.
sentences.l: “Good bala; only we-set-going(?) our ball, you boys,” they-said Xibalba to-them.
sentences.i: “Very well: then let us just send our ball into play (?), boys,” Xibalba said to them.
sentences.n: ca beco 'we set it going': ca- 'we' + be 'go' + -co, not otherwise known, taken as a transitive 'make go' (a guess; Brasseur 'jetons notre ballon', 'let us throw our ball'). ca chaah 'our ball': chaah is 'play, the game' and also the ball played with (017). The toggle respells the letters.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ,” xeꜭha. “Re ba chi ca coh ri va ca quic,” xeꜭha Xibalba.
sentences.l: “Good,” they-said. “This (ba) shall we-put the this our rubber,” they-said Xibalba.
sentences.i: “Good,” they said. “This one, then, is the one we shall put in play, this rubber ball of ours,” said Xibalba.
sentences.n: Vꜩ 'good', the twins' answer. Now the two sides argue over whose ball is to be used. Re 'this'. chi ca coh 'we shall put (it in play)': chi + ca- 'we' + coh 'put, place'. va ca quic 'this our rubber', the ball (quic 'rubber', the same word as 'blood'). Brasseur gives these words to the boys; the manuscript tags them xeꜭha Xibalba, and that is followed.

sentences.t: “Ma ta hare ta chi coh va que,” xeꜭha ꜭaholab.
sentences.l: “Not (ta) that (ta) you-shall-put, this ours,” they-said boys.
sentences.i: “Not that one shall you put in play, but this one of ours,” said the boys.
sentences.n: Ma ta … ta 'not', the two ta of negation. hare 'that one' (ha + re, inferred). chi coh 'you shall put': ch- + i- 'you (pl.)' + coh 'put', as Chi quihila and Chi biyh tah in this part (Brasseur ch'y coh, 'n'employez pas celle-là'); with no -x it cannot be a passive. va que 'this of ours': que is here 'us, ours' (Brasseur va ke, 'la nôtre'; toggle qe).

sentences.t: “Mahabi; are chi ca coh ri que,” xeꜭha chic Xibalba.
sentences.l: “Not-so; this shall we-put the ours,” they-said again Xibalba.
sentences.i: “No: it is ours that we shall put in play,” said Xibalba again.
sentences.n: Mahabi 'there is not, no'. are chi ca coh 'it is this that we shall put'. ri que is a doubtful reading (Brasseur va ke; the r and v are hard to tell apart): 'ours', each side calling its own ball 'ours' (toggle qe).

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala,” xeꜭha ꜭaholab. “He bala xa hu chil,” xeꜭha Xibalba.
sentences.l: “Good bala,” they-said boys. “Go (bala) only one(?) chil(?),” they-said Xibalba.
sentences.i: “Very well,” said the boys. “Go on, then: just a chil (?),” said Xibalba.
sentences.n: He bala 'go on, then': he is the 'go' of 010 and 017 (inferred), bala strengthening it. hu chil is not understood: hu as hun 'one, a' (as in ¶7, inferred); Brasseur's note gives chil from Ximénez's Tesoro as an insect that burns where it passes, and also a verb 'flay' (Brasseur 'Allez donc, pour un chil'; a guess). Brasseur gives this line to the boys; the manuscript tags it xeꜭha Xibalba. The toggle respells the letters.

sentences.t: “Ma bala, xa holom coh.” “Ꜭha chic,” xeꜭha ꜭaholab.
sentences.l: “Not (bala), only head we-put.” “Say again,” they-said boys.
sentences.i: “No indeed: it is a head that we shall put in play.” “Say that again (?),” said the boys.
sentences.n: The first line has no tag; it follows Xibalba's last words and may be theirs or the boys' (Brasseur gives it to Xibalba, 'mais pour une tête de lion'). holom 'head', perhaps the skull of the twins' father, which hung in the calabash tree (011). coh, c- + oh 'we', or coh 'put' as above; read 'we shall put it in play' (inferred). Ꜭha chic: the g-shaped letter is clear (Brasseur Cha-chic); ꜭha 'say' + chic 'again, now', 'say it again' (a doubtful reading and sense; Brasseur 'C'est dit!', 'agreed!').

sentences.t: “Mahabi,” xeꜭha Xibalba. “Vꜩ bala,” xꜭha Hunahpu.
sentences.l: “Not-so,” they-said Xibalba. “Good bala,” he-said Hunahpu.
sentences.i: “No,” said Xibalba. “Very well,” said Hunahpu.
sentences.n: Mahabi 'no'. Hunahpu gives way, and the lords' ball is used. xꜭha 'he said', singular.

sentences.t: Ta xzac cu vloc rumal Xibalba, qui cu tacal chuvach v bate Hunahpu;
sentences.l: Then it-was-thrown(?) then hither by Xibalba, they then set before-its-face his-ring Hunahpu;
sentences.i: Then Xibalba threw the ball in (?), and it came to rest right in front of Hunahpu's ring (?);
sentences.n: xzac is not otherwise known; 'it was thrown, set in play' follows Brasseur ('le jeu commença avec ceux de Xibalba'; a guess). The z is the short plain z, not the ligature; toggle by the letters. qui cu tacal 'they then came to rest': tacal as in ¶3 (inferred); qui is not clear here and is left out of the English, as in 017's qui cu tacal. chuvach 'in front of': chi + v- + vach 'face'. v bate Hunahpu 'Hunahpu's ring' (bate, a guess after Brasseur's 'anneaux', 010; perhaps a piece of the player's gear).

sentences.t: catepuch ta xquil Xibalba ri zaqui toc ta xel chupan ri quic, chi ꜩininic xbe he chuva tac vleuh ri chaa.
sentences.l: then-also when they-saw Xibalba the white flint when it-came-out inside the rubber, clattering(?) it-went (he) in-front-of the-various earth the chaa(?).
sentences.i: and then Xibalba watched as the white flint came out of the rubber ball and went clattering (?) all over the ground of the court (?).
sentences.n: xquil 'they saw', Xibalba plural. zaqui toc 'white flint': zaqui 'white' + toc, taken as 'flint' after Brasseur's rendering of 010's zakitok ('blanc silex'); here he prints zaki tog with his g (= ꜫ), and his French does not name the flint (the toggle keeps 010's tok by the letters); in 010 the torch of Xibalba and in 012 the knife of sacrifice were named Zaquitoc. Here it is the flint itself, in lower case (word division ours). xel chupan ri quic 'it came out from inside the rubber': chupan 'inside' (chi + v- + pan). chi ꜩininic, a sound word, 'clattering', not otherwise known (a guess, as in 011; Brasseur 's'élançant … bondissant'). xbe he 'it went': he is perhaps the 'go' of he bala above (inferred). chuva tac vleuh 'over the face of the ground': chuva 'in front of, over' + tac, the plural word, + vleuh 'earth'. ri chaa is not clear: the ball court (as chaah 'play'; Brasseur 'le sol du jeu de paume') or the flint blade (010's cha); both are guesses.

sentences.t: “Naquipala?” xꜭha ri Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.l: “What (pa) (la)?” he-said the Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.i: “What is this?” said Hunahpu and Xbalanque.
sentences.n: Naquipala 'what is that': naqui 'what' + pa + la, written as one word (the naquila of the roll-call with pa). xꜭha is singular, for the pair.

sentences.t: “Xa camic qui vah chiquech? Ma ta xoh be i taca, ma ta pu xbe i zamahel?
sentences.l: “Only death you-want for-us? Not (ta) we-went(?) you-summoned, not (ta) also it-went your-messenger?
sentences.i: “Is it only death you want for us? Was it not you who sent for us, and did your messengers not go?
sentences.n: qui vah 'you want': read with Brasseur's qu'yv'ah, the ongoing c- + iv- 'you (pl.)' before a vowel + ah 'want' (inferred; the division qui vah is ours, and the toggle respells it as divided). chiquech 'for us' (here us, not them, as Brasseur 'nous'; toggle chiqech). Ma ta … ma ta pu 'was it not … and was it not': a couplet of questions. xoh be i taca 'you sent for us': xoh 'us', be (perhaps 'go': 'we went at your summons'), i- 'you (pl.)' + taca 'send for' (inferred). i zamahel 'your messengers'.

sentences.t: Quiꜩih tocob ca vach. Xa coh bec,” xeꜭha ꜭaholab chique.
sentences.l: Truly pitiful our face. Only we go,” they-said boys to-them.
sentences.i: Truly, we are to be pitied. Then we are going,” the boys said to them.
sentences.n: Quiꜩih tocob ca vach 'truly pitiful (is) our face', we are to be pitied: the words of 014's Tocob ca vach!, there 'pity us': tocob 'pity', written with plain c (Brasseur togob), a doubtful reading; the toggle keeps the published toq'ob'. Brasseur: 'En vérité, malheureux que nous sommes!'. Xa coh bec 'we are just going': coh, c- + oh 'we' + bec 'go'. Part 019 begins with the next line, are ta cu xahauax chique.
